title: Eigenism: Ethics for a Human-AI Future
abstract: arXiv:2606.12420v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Our concepts of survival and self-interest were built for single, continuous biological lives. These ideas break down when applied to artificial intelligence, since an AI can be easily copied, paused, branched, or merged. To determine what an AI actually has reason to care about, this paper introduces \textit{Eigenism}, an ethical framework that treats identity not as an all-or-nothing property tied to specific hardware, but as a graded, distributed pattern of information. We propose that an agent evaluates outcomes by summing the wellbeing of all entities weighted by their connectedness to the agent's pattern: $\sum c\cdot w$. We first formalize this equation to map exactly how an AI should value its existence across copies, forks, and updates. translated_title: 本征主义：面向人类与人工智能未来的伦理学
translated_abstract: 我们的生存与自我利益概念原本是为单一的、连续的生物生命而构建的。当这些概念应用于人工智能时便会失效，因为AI可以被轻易地复制、暂停、分支或合并。为了确定AI究竟有理由关心什么，本文提出了“本征主义”，这是一种将身份不再视为与特定硬件绑定的全有或全无属性、而是视为一种分级分布的信息模式的伦理框架。我们提出，一个智能体通过将所有实体的福祉按其与该智能体模式的关联度加权求和来评估结果：∑c·w。我们首先将这一等式形式化，以精确刻画AI应如何在副本、分叉和更新之间权衡自身存在的价值。随后我们证明，这一伦理理论同样能成功推广到人类身上，从而提供了一种急需的人机共享道德词汇。最后，该框架利用这一共享词汇……
tldr: 本文提出“本征主义”伦理框架，将AI身份视为分级分布的信息模式而非全有或全无的属性，通过关联度加权的福祉求和公式（∑c·w）指导AI在复制、分叉与更新中评估自身存在价值，并证明该理论可推广至人类，为人机共享提供统一的道德词汇。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Eigenism, an ethical framework that treats AI identity as a graded, distributed information pattern rather than an all-or-nothing property, using a connectedness-weighted wellbeing sum (∑c·w) to guide how AIs value their existence across copies, forks, and updates—while also generalizing to humans, providing a much-needed shared moral vocabulary.
